members.note: One UDreamPanelSlot class for every panel instead of a slot class per panel, so there is nothing to cast. GetPanelSlot / CreateNewPanelSlot / HasPanelSlots are the verbs.
Drawn by UDreamUITooltipSubsystem, which resolves the nearest ancestor offering text or a tooltip widget.

A CLASS, not an instance: the tooltip service instantiates its content when the bubble appears and destroys it when the bubble goes, so nothing is kept alive per host for a bubble shown seconds at a time.

Split into RenderTranslation / RenderRotation / RenderScale / RenderTransformPivot / RenderShear, and 3D rather than UMG's FWidgetTransform, because the authored transform it mirrors is FVector/FQuat/FVector. RenderShear is stored apart from the other three and is NOT part of HasRenderTransform: those three compose into an FTransform and a shear cannot survive that trip, so it is applied on the matrix path instead.
Normalized in the widget's own rect with (0,0) at bottom-left, matching AnchorData.Pivot rather than UMG's top-left origin.

EDreamFlowDirectionPreference mirrors EFlowDirectionPreference value for value. GetResolvedFlowDirection is the resolved answer; a tree that states nothing reads left to right, because DreamGUI never joins Slate's paint pass and so cannot read GSlateFlowDirection meaningfully.

AND-ed into the existing three-valued Interactable cascade, so GetInteractableInHierarchy -- which input, navigation and every control's disabled look already read -- is the single answer. A disabled ancestor outranks a descendant pinned Interactable=Enabled. GetIsEnabledInHierarchy is the cascaded query.

There is no Slate accessible-widget layer here to take defaults FROM: a DreamGUI widget is a mesh, not an SWidget, so accessibility is the AccessibleBehavior/AccessibleText pair on the widget itself and there is nothing for an override flag to switch between.
Same reason: no accessible widget tree is built, so there is no child accessibility to suppress. AccessibleBehavior=NotAccessible is the per-widget answer.
EDreamAccessibleBehavior mirrors ESlateAccessibleBehavior's Auto/NotAccessible/Summary/Custom.
One behaviour covers both texts here rather than two: AccessibleBehavior=Summary announces AccessibleSummaryText, Custom announces AccessibleText.
Volatility is a Slate invalidation-panel concept -- 'do not cache this widget's draw elements'. DreamGUI rebuilds draw calls from its own dirty flags and has no cached element list to opt out of.
Resolved per frame by DreamPointerPolicy::ResolveCursor over the hover stack, innermost first; EMouseCursor::Default means 'no opinion', which is why there is no separate bOverride_Cursor.
EDreamWidgetClipping mirrors EWidgetClipping; ClippingCornerRadius and ClippingMargin are extra.

EDreamWidgetVisibility maps ESlateVisibility one for one (Visible/Hidden/Collapsed/HitTestInvisible/SelfHitTestInvisible). Hit testing is additionally gated by Raycastable, which has no UMG counterpart, and by WidgetActive, which is the behaviour lifecycle switch.
The engine's own EWidgetPixelSnapping type.
Inherited down the tree here; GetFinalRenderOpacity is the accumulated answer.
The per-direction rules live on a UDreamWidgetNavigation behaviour, as UMG hangs them off a UWidgetNavigation object. GetNavigation reads it, GetOrCreateNavigation makes one.
Four channel setters instead of one FWidgetTransform: SetRenderTranslation, SetRenderRotation, SetRenderScale, SetRenderTransformPivot, plus ClearRenderTransform to put them all back.
Takes an FVector, not an FVector2D: this framework's widgets are 3D and world-space canvases exist.

Rides the matrix path that a perspective scope already uses, because a perspective remap IS a shear and the vertex transform had to grow that branch for it. An unsheared tree still takes the FTransform branch, byte for byte. Two differences from UMG, both noted on the property: layout never sees it, and HIT TESTING DOES NOT FOLLOW -- the raycaster switches to the matrix only inside a perspective scope, so a sheared widget is clicked on its un-slanted rect.
Writes the Roll channel of RenderRotation -- depth runs along local X here, so roll is the rotation that keeps a widget flat against the canvas. Pitch and yaw are left alone.
Takes an FVector. Negative X brings a widget toward the viewer.
This widget's own switch; GetIsEnabledInHierarchy is the cascaded answer.
Virtual, as UMG's is. Cascades through GetInteractableInHierarchy, which is what input, navigation and the controls' disabled look already read.
Walks up to the nearest tracked page, because the caller is usually a widget several levels inside one.
By class rather than by instance; see the ToolTipWidget row.
Back to EMouseCursor::Default, which here means 'no opinion' rather than 'force the arrow'.
Visible AND contributing colour: a subtree faded to zero opacity is visible but not rendered.
The hierarchy is folded in, unlike UMG's, which asks only the widget itself. The cascaded answer is the one already cached and the one callers mean by 'on screen'.
GetFinalRenderOpacity is the same value with ancestors folded in.
See bIsVolatile: there is no cached Slate element list to opt a widget out of.
True for the widget under the pointer and for every ancestor it entered through, which is what Slate's hover propagation gives UMG for free. Asked of the owning player's event system.
Moved down from UDreamUserWidget so any widget can answer it. Uses the owning player's index rather than player zero.
The same answer as GetIsFocusable, under UMG's name.
There is no capture object here; a pointer still holding its button down on this widget is what capture means to a caller -- its drags and its release come here regardless of what it moves over.
Pointer index -1 means any of that player's pointers, as in UMG.
Returns bool rather than UMG's void -- the pre-existing signature in this framework, kept.
Asks every local player's event system.
Strictly descendants, as in UMG.
Pre-existing, with UserIndex and PointerId defaulted, so a Blueprint calls it with no arguments as in UMG. Returns false when the widget cannot take focus.
Returns bool rather than void, matching SetFocus in this framework.
The widget's own face on what UDreamUIBPLibrary::ForceLayoutPrepass already did.
The layout half only; the volatility half is rejected for the reason on bIsVolatile.
Answered by the parent panel, because measuring is a conversation between a container and its child. A widget with no measuring parent reports the size it has.
Reach the component with UDreamWidget::GetOrCreateNavigation.
Null clears the direction back to Escape.

EDreamUINavigationRule::CustomBoundary, added at the END of the enum so no serialized value moved. The scan runs first and the delegate is asked only when it found nothing in that direction -- which is what 'the move left the area' means here. Distinct from Custom, which is asked for every move and so has to answer the ordinary steps too.
Returns a UDreamWidget: any widget can take children here, so there is no separate panel class to return.
Leaves the widget alive and parked, and frees its screen-page name if it had one.

FDreamUIWidgetGeometry stands in for FGeometry. There is one geometry rather than three, because there is no deferred paint pass to lag behind the tick -- see the GetTickSpaceGeometry and GetPaintSpaceGeometry rows.
Same value as GetCachedGeometry: DreamGUI arranges and draws in one pass, so tick space and paint space cannot disagree.
Same value as GetCachedGeometry, for the same reason.
Field notification is implemented by UDreamUserWidget, which is what a Blueprint author subclasses; a bare UDreamWidget has no compiled field list to notify about.

BlueprintInternalUseOnly, as UMG marks it: the node an author uses is the one a field-notify property generates, not this by-name call. Same two guards as the add and the remove -- an id naming no field on this class is an authoring mistake, not a broadcast to nobody.
Virtual on UDreamWidget; UDreamUserWidget overrides it to check an explicitly set controller first.
